section_summary: This section records requests, schedule changes, and government replies concerning visits by Japanese naval vessels and transports to California and Hawaii in late 1939. It also contains correspondence about cargo loaded on Japanese public vessels without export documentation, followed by a complaint and newspaper clipping about a sentry aboard Yakumo at Hilo.

subfiles.title: Treasury opinion on cargo aboard Erimo
subfiles.about: Addresses export manifests and customs privileges for cargo loaded aboard the Japanese naval tanker Erimo.
subfiles.summary: Treasury says Commerce must decide manifest requirements, while State must decide whether cargo loading abuses granted courtesies. It seeks a customs report on whether scrap tin was restricted tinplate scrap.

subfiles.title: Definition of usual customs courtesies
subfiles.from: Stephen B. Gibbons, Assistant Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.to: J. M. Johnson, Assistant Secretary of Commerce
subfiles.about: Explains customary treatment of visiting foreign government ships.
subfiles.summary: Describes a welcome, courteous landing of personnel, and no official vessel inspection.

subfiles.title: State Department view on Japanese vessels’ cargo
subfiles.from: R. Walton Moore, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.to: Harry L. Hopkins, Secretary of Commerce
subfiles.about: Addresses undocumented cargo loaded aboard Erimo and a Japanese training vessel in Hawaii.
subfiles.summary: State concludes that customs courtesies do not permit foreign public vessels to load export cargo without required manifests, clearances, or licenses. Because time has elapsed, it will not formally raise the past incidents with Japan, but asks that future violations be stopped and reported. It awaits the Honolulu collector’s report on scrap tin.

subfiles.title: Transmittal to Treasury concerning Japanese cargo
subfiles.from: Counselor, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau Jr., Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.about: Sends Treasury a copy of State’s letter to Commerce.
subfiles.summary: Requests the Honolulu customs collector’s report when available.

subfiles.title: Complaint concerning Japanese armed sentries
subfiles.about: Protests an armed Japanese sentry and visitor procedures during the Hilo visit.
subfiles.summary: The writer objects to visitors being asked to bow to a sentry aboard Yakumo and encloses a newspaper account of a customs inspector’s encounter.

subfiles.title: Advertiser clipping on Yakumo sentry incident
subfiles.about: Reports claims that visitors to Yakumo were asked to salute or bow to a sentry.
subfiles.summary: A photograph and article describe a sign aboard Yakumo and a reported refusal by customs inspector H. S. Wilson to bow. The State Department awaits a customs report. The clipping also contains unrelated newspaper stories and a report of a missing Yakumo sailor.

subfiles.title: Reply to Arno Hellthaler
subfiles.from: Maxwell M. Hamilton, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the complaint and enclosed report about Yakumo’s sentry.
subfiles.summary: States that the letter and clipping have been noted.
